sources.citation: Li Jinfang 李锦芳 & Jerold Edmondson 艾杰瑞. 2006. 中越边境的红仡佬语及其初步比较 [Red Gelao of the China-Vietnam border and a preliminary comparison]. Conference paper, 民族语言国际学术研讨会, Lijiang (archived from ling.uta.edu/~jerry/)
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Describes Malipo Red Gelao (redg1235), not Qau: 5 tones and progressive tone assimilation; nothing on stress. Kept only for the record.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. [2004 web draft]. Kra or Kadai languages. 10 pp. (draft of the chapter published in Diller, Edmondson & Luo eds. 2008, The Tai-Kadai Languages, Routledge), archived from ling.uta.edu/~jerry/
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Gelao section: 'typically four tones (Wanzi has six)', uvulars, prenasalization, loss of codas, Wanzi wordlist; no stress statement for Gelao (only Buyang is said to have 'sesqui-syllabic structure with the first syllable being toneless').

sources.citation: Ostapirat, Weera. 2000. Proto-Kra. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 23(1): 1-251. (image-only scan; pdf pp. 1-40 scanned here, pp. 1-60 already scanned in../laha1250/ocr_ost)
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Comparative-historical reconstruction; sec. 2.6 (pp. 26-28) treats Wanzi (Central) and Dagouchang Gelao initials/tones from He 1983 and Zhang 1993; no statement about word stress anywhere in the pages read (chapters 1-2, start of ch. 3).

sources.citation: Coyaud, Maurice. 1987. Les langues dans le monde chinois. Paris: Pour l'Analyse du Folklore. pp. 161-162, sec. 3.7 'Gelao' (Rosetta Project extract, archive.org rosettaproject_gio_phon-1)

sources.note: Lists six tones (55, 44, 33, 24, 13, 31), initials, finals and consonant clusters; nothing on stress/accent.

sources.citation: He Jiashan 贺嘉善. 1983. 仡佬语简志 (Gelaoyu jianzhi) [A sketch of Gelao]. Beijing: 民族出版社. 107 pp. — 语音 chapter (声母/韵母/声调/音节), based on Wanzi 湾子寨, Anshun (= wanz1234 under qaua1234).

sources.note: The standard primary description of exactly this variety; jianzhi phonology chapters routinely note 轻声/weakly-read prefix syllables and sandhi; Yang 2008 uses it as baseline.

sources.note: Acoustic study of mono-, di- and trisyllabic words in Anshun (Wanzi/Heizhai) Gelao with 16 speakers; likely reports duration/F0 asymmetries between syllables (prominence) and sandhi domains.

sources.citation: Zhou Guoyan 周国炎. 2004. 仡佬族母语生态研究 [Studies on the mother-tongue ecology of the Gelao]. Beijing: 民族出版社. — phonological sketches of Anshun (Wanzi/Heizhai) and Dagouchang Gelao incl. tone sandhi (pp. ~55-64).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: First-hand tone system (5 tones) and sandhi rules for Anshun Gelao quoted by Yang 2008; may state which syllable keeps full tone in disyllables.

sources.citation: Zhang Jimin 张济民. 1993. 仡佬语研究 [A study of Gelao]. Guiyang: 贵州民族出版社. 4+3+542 pp. — 语音 chapters; representative point Pingba Dagouchang 平坝大狗场 (= Qau); see esp. p. 378 (轻声调, cited by Bo Wenze 2003) and the discussion of 前加成分 taking 轻声调.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Largest description; snippets show it explicitly discusses a light/neutral tone on prefix syllables 'in most Gelao points' — the closest thing to a word-prominence statement for Dagouchang.
